articleTitle: Subsurface Object Recognition in a Soil Using UWB Irradiation by Butterfly Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of recognition of a cylindrical perfectly conducting object buried in a soil is solving by artificial neural network that takes data from subsurface radar with the use of impulse electromagnetic wave. The air-ground interface is irradiated by the butterfly antenna excited with ultrawideband short impulse current. Electromagnetic problem is solved by FDTD simulation. The results of the calculation in form of time dependences of differently polarized electrical components of received fields in four points are used for artificial neural network training for determination of the cylinder placement. The recognition abilities of the network are verified by noisy input data with different levels of additive Gaussian noise and received for shifted positions of receiver.

articleTitle: Influence of Noise Reduction on Object Location Classification by Artificial Neural Networks for UWB Subsurface Radiolocation
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The practical application of subsurface radars in ultrawideband radiolocation is restricted by a presence of noise in the received signal. The phenomenon creates important limitations on the precision of the data acquired because of low energy of electromagnetic field components generated by subsurface objects of interests in comparison with the incident and reflected from air-ground interface waves. Although the artificial neural networks used to recognize hidden objects have their own abilities to resist the noises and other harmful unpredictable deviations in real measurements of impulse electromagnetic wave the influence of previous denoising is investigated. It is compared the results of object classification of its position by artificial neural network for noisy data of different noise levels and preliminary processed by wavelet transform and caterpillar method of denoising.

articleTitle: Numerical analysis of wave scattering by periodic systems of impedance tapes
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Computer modeling of investigated problem was conducted. It was based on numerical solution of obtained singular integral equations. The results of computer calculations were compared with the results of computational experiments conducted using analysis of hypersingular integral equations.

articleTitle: Extemal Parameters of Wireless Power Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The report outlines a procedure for analyzing wireless power transfer system (WPT) intended for determining the system parameters, describing interaction of the WPT system with other electronic systems and the processes occurring within the system.

articleTitle: A Formulaic Model Calculating the Permittivity of Testing Materials Placed on a Circular Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this study, a formulaic model optimized by artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm is presented for calculation of the relative permittivity of testing materials which placed on a coaxial-fed circular patch antenna (CPA). The CPA with patch diameter of 34 mm and thickness of 1.6 mm is designed for operating at a resonant frequency of 2.37 GHz. Solid materials to be tested, having a thickness of 2 mm and the patch diameter size, are placed on the antenna patch. Therefore, the resonant frequency and the quality factor of the CPA with the material would change depending on the permittivity of the solid material. The resonant frequency and the quality factor of the CPA with various solid materials (the relative permittivity from 1 to 100) are obtained by simulations. An optimum model is fitted by the ABC through the simulation data for calculation of the permittivity of testing solid material. The model is also verified over the calculated permittivity for three testing materials. Therefore, the permittivity of a testing material can be accurately determined by the model without using numerical or analytical electromagnetic solutions.

articleTitle: The Exponential and Polynomial Approximations of the Fermi-Dirac Integral
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The approximations of Fermi-Dirac integral are examined. The exponential and combined exponential- polynomial models are investigated. The modifications of the Prony method are proposed. The errors of the different approaches are compared.

articleTitle: Experimental Studies of the Fabry-Perot Resonator with Mirrors Perforated by Coaxial-Sector Holes
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper presents theoretical and experimental studies of the Fabry-Perot resonator, consisting of flat, mutually parallel mirrors, of finite thickness, perforated by coaxial-sector holes. The comparative analysis of the experimental and theoretical frequency characteristics of the reflection coefficients for a single mirror and system of two mirrors is presented. The occurrence of the transmission resonance of an electromagnetic wave for two mirrors system at a wavelength less than cut-off wavelength is experimentally confirmed.

articleTitle: Interaction of the Crack and Thin Elastic Layer in the Solid Under Time-Harmonic Loading
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Steady state vibrations in 3D solid consisting of two elastic half-spaces, intermediate thin layer and containing in one of the half-spaces penny-shaped crack is considered. The solution is selected as integral representation with unknown crack-opening functions. Formulated problem in frequency domain is solved by a boundary integral equation method (BIEM). The influence of applied loading frequency, the ratio of the stiffness of the solid materials, the crack depth on mode-III dynamic stress intensity factor (SIF) near crack front points is investigated.

articleTitle: Modeling of Soil’s Cavity EM Response
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Paper presents results of computer modeling based on The Method of Auxiliary Sources. It is considered cavity's EM response in soil, in wide frequency range and different values of soil's electrical conductivity. The research is related to studding of the detection abilities of anti-personnel plastic mines by EM exposure.

articleTitle: Shelled Plasmonic Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Plasmonic structures attract much interest because they present exotic properties in areas that are much smaller than a wavelength. They are attractive for different applications such as sensors, single molecule detection, near- field microscopy, enhanced Raman spectroscopy, etc. At optical frequencies, metals act as a dielectric with negative permittivity and they lose their conductivity and become dispersive and lossy. As plasmonic structures are dispersive materials wich have a complicate frequency response so it is more convenient to simulate electromagnetic processes using frequency domain numerical methods. In this paper Method of Auxiliary Sources are presented as a numerical technique for simulation. MAS is frequency domain numerical solver of electromagnetic fields, which needs less computer resources then other numerical methods.

articleTitle: Numerical Efficiency of Methods for Electromagnetic Transmission Problem with Analytical Regularization
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: in this work electromagnetic transmission problem is considered with purpose to build fast and efficient numerical algorithm which leads to numerical simulation software development to model plasmonic nanoantennas. Spectral Fourier-Galerkin method is used in conjunction with novel technique of boundary parametrization. Analytical regularization based on technique of singularity subtraction is corrected leading to exponential rate of convergence not only for smooth boundaries, but also for polygonal domains. Numerical simulation software tool allows accurate investigation of nearfield characteristics as well as far-field characteristics, even in situations when other methods are not able to do so.

articleTitle: Spectral Surface Integral Equation Method for Plasmonic Nanostructures
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: When design of antenna relies on results of experimental research, this makes designing hugely expensive. To solve numerically the scattering problem which rises from antenna simulations, in this work a novel technique of surface parameterization in conjunction with spectral Galerkin Boundary Integral Equation (BIE) method with analytical regularization based on singularity division technique and Fast Fourier Transforms (FFT) for numerical integration of all Galerkin coefficients simultaneously is applied for the first time to solve this class of problems.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Reactive Fields’ Some Properties
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: During solution of the practical problems related to the construction of the field radiators or receivers, the important problem is to “match” them with the free space. The bad matching leads to the formation of the undesired reactive field in the near zone of the corresponding antenna. The investigations show that, the best matching can be achieved by putting the sources in the points of singularities of the far field's analytical continuation. By this could be achieve the minimalarea of the reactive field. If the sources, which describes the far field, are distributed outside the singularities, then in the near zone the reactive field with the high amplitude is created, which doesn't make such a radiator optimal. In the given work the sources are distributed initially outside the singularity points. The goal is to study main properties of the excited reactive field and to study the far field formation mechanism, when the sources of the radiation are singularities points out.

articleTitle: Singularities’ Distribution of the Field’s Analytical Continuation, Scattered by the Front Part of the Mirror Sphere
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this article there is investigated the character of the singularities' distribution corresponding to the analytical continuation of the field reflected by the front part of the perfect electric conductor sphere illuminated by the electromagnetic waves point source. The analysis of these singularities show, that they represent the distorted image of the incident wave source and are distributed on the caustic surface. The discrete character of the singularities, when the ratio of the sphere radius and the incident wave length is finite, is explained by the Fresnel zone method. The numerical experiments performed to determine the scattered field's singularities confirm theoretical reasoning based on geometrical optics and Fresnel's zone method.

articleTitle: The Effect of Cylindricity and Coaxiality Deviations of Samples on Measurement Error of the Permittivity Using a Biconical Resonator
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the measurement of permittivity by biconical resonator. The effect of the cylindrical and coaxial deviations of test samples on the parameters of the biconical resonator and the accuracy of measuring permittivity are studied. The resonance frequency shift due to variations of factors of deviation of cylindricity and coaxiality are obtained. Estimations of effects are carried out numerically. To ensure acceptable accuracy of permittivity measurement, requirements for the quality of sample fabrication are formulated.

articleTitle: Determination of Parameters of Equivalent Model of a Periodic Structure Using Frequency-Time DomainTransformations
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of representing S-parameters of a periodic structure using the model of an equivalent homogeneous layer is considered. For correct determination of the values of the parameters for such model, it is proposed to use the transition to the time domain and inverse one using the Fourier transform. The use of the proposed approach has been examined for several types of periodic structures. The efficiency of this approach is shown for periodic structures with frequency bands of the anomalous behavior of the phase-frequency characteristic.

articleTitle: Design of Quad-port Circular MIMO Antenna With Isolation Improved by Shorting Walls
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A compact co-located quad-port circular multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system operating at a wide frequency range of 3. 0 - 5.0 GHz is designed in this study. The antenna system comprises a 20 mm radius circular patch composed of four co-located elements fed by 50 Ohm probe and a 50 x50mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ground plane. To alleviate the mutual coupling among the antenna elements, the circular patch is split into four quadrants using two orthogonal shorting walls (SWs). In order to further improve the impedance matching, two circular slots are etched on the edge of the elements. The mutual coupling reducing performance of the SW is examined through the surface current and E-field distributions. The performance analysis of the MIMO system, regarding the radiation patterns, envelope-correlation-coefficient (ECC) and peak gain is thoroughly investigated. The antenna system is eligible for especially the access points due to being compact and versatile.

articleTitle: SH-waves Reflection and Transmission by a Periodic Array of Piezoelectric Inclusions in an Elastic Medium
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A method for analysis of SH-waves scattering by a periodic array of thin piezoelectric inclusions in an infinite elastic solid is presented. We assume that inclusions have the same material properties and shape. Ideal mechanical contact and electric insulation are imposed on the boundary of each inhomogeneity. The method is based on Fourier transformation method and singular perturbations modeling of interaction between host material and fillers. Influence of geometric characteristics of the array and electromechanical coupling on frequency dependencies of reflection and transmission coefficients is analyzed.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Two-Parameter Spectral Problems in Studies of Solutions of Differential and Nonlinear Integral Equations of Hammerstein Type
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The theory and methods of solving the nonlinear multi-parametric spectral problems and their application in investigations of spectral properties of linear differential equations, which comprise the spectral parameters in equation coefficients and boundary conditions nonlinearly, are considered. Investigation of the problem of non-uniqueness of solutions to the non-linear integral equations of the Hammerstein type, which are used in the theory of the synthesis of antennas with a plane radiating aperture, is presented. A number of numerical examples of solving specific spectral problems are given.

articleTitle: The Inverse Problem for Determination of Surface Emissivity and Reflectivity of a Layer of Low Thermal Conductivity
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An inverse problem for simultaneous determination of the emissivity and reflectivity of a layer of small thermal conductivity on the base of data obtained by measuring surface temperature and energy flux flowing out the layer through its surface has been considered.

articleTitle: Acoustic Wave Scattering by Coplanar System of Flat Pre Fractal Impedance Strips Gratings
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The singular integral equation technique and local coordinate system method are used for mathematical modelling of acoustic waves' scattering by multi level coplanar system of flat pre-fractal impedance strip gratings. Main attention is focussed on some types of one-dimensional self similar fractals with variable fractal dimension. It is important to have huge sets of pre-fractals for usage in construction of flat pre-fractal impedance strip gratings. The simplest two level coplanar system of pre-fractal grating is studied in detail. In particular, asymptotic model of the acoustic wave scattering by such weakly filled system, which has explicit solution, is presented.

articleTitle: Frequency Spectrum and Electromagnetic Fields Distribution in Cavity Microwave Resonator with Metal Pins Inside
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An experimental and numerical research of the frequency spectrum probabilistic properties and electromagnetic field distribution in a cavity cylindrical microwave resonator has been performed. We made this research for three possible cases of a singular inhomogeneity's location in the resonator's cavity: the absence of inhomogeneities, the symmetric location of the inhomogeneities, and an asymmetric location of inhomogeneities. We worked with microwave resonator at the centimeter and millimeter wavebands. Resonator had the form of an aluminum hollow cylinder with two circular sourced holes in its sidewall. Brass pins were used as singular inhomogeneities. Diameter of pins is equivalent to the wavelength at the upper limit of the working frequency range. Numerical simulating calculations were performed using the CST Microwave Studio. The aim of numerical research is to confirm the experimental results for a similar model of the resonator system. Frequency spectra data were obtained using experimental and simulation results. We built the probability distribution of the inter-frequency intervals to determine signs of wave chaos in the studied resonator with inhomogeneities. We found the Poisson distribution in the probability distribution of the inter-frequency intervals in the case of the empty microwave cavity resonator (without pins) and in the case when metal pins inside the microwave cavity has symmetrical location relatively to the central axis of the resonator. In the case, when metal pins are located asymmetrically, the probability distribution of inter-frequency intervals becomes similar to the Wigner distribution.

articleTitle: Application of Regularizing Algorithms for Solving Ill-conditioned LAS Arising in Problems of Scatterer Form Reconsttuction
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The algorithms enabled to regularize the ill-posed problems of body form reconstruction are proposed and tested. The first of them is based on the usual Tikhonov regularization and presents the iterative procedure, which minimize the deviation of the obtained form of scatterer on the desired one in the each iteration. The second one is based on the known dynamical system method allows to obtain the scatterer with form, norm of with is as close as possible to the norm of the desired form. The effectiveness of both the algorithms is compared at the different geometries of problem.

articleTitle: Full Wave Simulation of a Vertically Polarized Transverse Electromagnetic Mode Cell
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Vertically Polarized Transverse Electromagnetic Mode (VTEM) cells may be used for immunity tests in vehicles. The tests are performed according to the ISO 11451-2 Standard. This work material describes a full wave approach for simulation of a VTEM cell. The investigation is performed in two stages. Firstly, the field uniformity and vertical polarization of the empty cell are verified. Secondly, the impact of the vehicle presence on the field structure inside the cell is examined. The simulation results are compared to measurements.

articleTitle: Expansion of Frequency Range of Microstrip Antennas
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Low-profile antennas, in particular microstrip antennas, are widely used in aircraft, spacecraft and other objects, where size, weight and an aerodynamic profile are constraint. Significant disadvantage of these antennas is a very narrow frequency band. The paper proposes a rigorous method for analyzing microstrip antennas and a method for expanding their working frequency band. The analysis is based on the idea of the antenna as a parallel connection of metal and slot radiators. To extend the frequency band in-phase currents are created in both radiators.

articleTitle: Formulation and Numerical Analysis of Acoustics Problems in Coupled Thermohydroelastic Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The coupled thermohydroelastic processes of acoustic wave and heat propagation in weak viscous fluid and elastic bodies form the basis of dissipative acoustics. The problems of dissipative acoustics have many applications in engineering practice, in particular in the development of appropriate medical equipment. This paper presents mathematical models for time and frequency domain problems in terms of unknown displacements and temperatures in both the fluid and the elastic body. Formulated corresponding variational problems and constructed numerical schemes for their solution based on the Galerkin approximations. The method of proving the well-posedness of the considered variational problems is proposed.

articleTitle: Scattering of E-Polarized Electromagnetic Wave by Slotted Cylinder with Coaxially Enclosed Dielectric-Coated Cylinder
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The boundary-value method is applied to the problem of electromagnetic scattering of a plane E-polarized wave by a slotted circular cylinder with a coaxially enclosed solid circular cylinder coated with dielectric; both cylinders are perfectly conducting. The solution is obtained in the form of a system of linear algebraic equations. An approximate analytical solution in long-wavelength range for the case of narrow slot opening is formulated. Using both the analytical and the accurate numerical solutions the scattering cross sections of the structure are analyzed for a selection of sample configurations, including the effects of a finite thickness of the slotted cylinder's wall. Shown that the scattering from such structure exhibits resonance features, while in long-wavelength range it is closely matching the scattering from an equivalent solid circular cylinder.

articleTitle: General Resonance Condition for Waveguide Junctions with Natural Dielectric Inserts
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A general resonant condition for rectangular waveguide junctions operating in the single mode regime of the main waveguide is formulated based on previously developed mathematical models. We will consider three types of junction with various side arms: semi-infinite waveguide oriented in line with main waveguide, T-oriented semi-infinite waveguide with an impedance end wall, and infinite perpendicularly oriented waveguide. The main waveguide is coupling with the side arm through a narrow slot, and it has a dielectric insert in the coupling region. The simulation results obtained for the waveguide junctions have shown that the resonant conditions allow to attain correct results without taking into account the imaginary part of permittivity of the insert material.

articleTitle: Control System Automation of the Sputtering Device WUP -5m for the Study of Wave Propagation in Complex Media
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper discusses a method for automating the technology of deposition of thin films by vacuum thermal spraying to study the propagation of electromagnetic waves in complex media. The analysis of the necessary equipment and the possibility of its modernization. A functional diagram of the device to bring the vacuum universal port (VUP-5M) installation into a working state is described. Consideration is given to the functional units of the device, their composition and principle of operation, and features are considered when designing the device. Similar solutions, their advantages and disadvantages are given, the rationality of their use is considered.

Author Keywords: technology of deposition of thin films

articleTitle: A Numerical Method for Solving the Antenna Synthesis Problem by Power Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The bounded solutions of the variational problem are investigated. The theorem of the existence of solutions is formulated. The convergence of a class of iterative methods is proved. The proposed methods have regularizing property.

articleTitle: Improvement of Directional Properties of Individual Radiators and Antenna Arrays by Dielectric Guiding Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The paper considers the results simulation of the directional properties of printed antennas with dielectric structures located in the nearest zone of the radiators. The influence of the shape of the dielectric structures on the coefficient of directional of the antennas are shown. Examples for single radiators and gratings based on them are considered. Presented results were obtained using the method of moments in FEKO medium for a disk patch antenna with different dielectric structures in the range of 2.45 GHz. The received results can be used in systems of telecommunications and technical vision.

articleTitle: Mathematical Models for Resonant Radiation of Plane Wave Packets on Layered, Cubically Polarizable Gratings – Existence of Solutions
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Based on a unified model developed by the authors in previous works, the investigation of resonant radiation pro- cesses of waves on a nonmagnetic, isotropic, linearly polarized (E-polarization), cubically polarizable, layered and (possibly) longitudinally periodic, dielectric structure, which is excited by a packet of plane waves, is continued. In this paper a first rigourous result on the existence of (exact) solutions of this model is demonstrated. Numerical results illustrating the dependence of the energy properties of the resonant wave radiation on the magnitude of the susceptibility parameter of the medium at the resonant excitation frequency complete the presentation.

articleTitle: The B. Z. Katsenelebaum’s Monographs
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A comparative review of monographs by B. Z. Katenelenbaum, published in Russian, English and Ukrainian languages during 1966-2012, has been made.

articleTitle: The Sum of the Series for the Current in the Leontovich’s Equation
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A new version of solving Leontovich's integral equation for a current in a linear radiator, performed in the form of a thin-walled straight metal cylinder with circular cross section, is considered. The solution is based on using the method of variation of constants and is reduced to the sequential multiplying of the terms by one and the same magnitude. The sum is compared with the first components of the series and with the results of other methods for solving the problem. Results for different radiator sizes are given.

articleTitle: Impulse Electromagnetic Wave Propagation in Kerr Medium
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The transient unidirectional electrical current uniformly distributed on plane disk is considered as a source of electromagnetic wave. The electrical strength vector is received by the evolutionary approach in the time domain. Perturbation theory is applied to estimate nonlinear effects in Kerr medium of transient ultrawideband wave radiated from the circle aperture in approximation of weak nonlinearity. The nonlinear correction to the strength vector electrical field is derived analytically in time domain. To illustrate the results the numerical simulations of the wave propagation in Kerr medium are carried out.

articleTitle: Directional Characteristics of In-phase Self-complementary Radiators
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Antennas with in-phase currents have higher electrical characteristics than ordinary antennas of metal wires with sinusoidal currents. The in-phase current distribution not only allows us to obtain a high level of antenna matching with the cable, but also significantly changes the antenna patterns. If the current distribution along the radiator is known, it is possible to determine the antenna directivity. Calculation is based on determination of power fluxes through each part of a sphere. Comparison of directional properties of radiators shows that radiators with in-phase currents allow obtaining a higher level of directivity, which is preserved in a wide range of frequencies. A similar method of extending the frequency range by including capacitive loads into metal radiators can be used in self-complementary antennas. The results of applying the described method to flat self-complementary antennas confirms its high efficiency.

articleTitle: Waveguide Millimeter Wave Measurement Cell with Minimum Reflection Coefficient for Complex Permittivity Determination of Bioactive Liquids
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An original waveguide millimeter wave measurement cell for complex permittivity determination of bioactive high loss liquids was studied numerically and experimentally. This measurement cell consisted of round metal waveguide, Teflon inserted and glass capillary with liquid under text inside. The main features of the measurement cell are as follows. Waveguide connections (matching elements) to input and output waveguides have minimum reflection coefficient. The capillary with the high loss liquids under test located not in the electromagnetic field maximum as usual, but at an angle to the wave propagation along the waveguide cell. The advantages of such capillary location were discussed in the paper. This waveguide millimeter wave measurement cell was compared with the symmetrical waveguide millimeter wave measurement cell for complex permittivity determination.

articleTitle: Microwave Methods for Monitoring Parameters of Dielectrics Developed in Ukraine: Overview
publicationTitle: 2019 XXIVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Some approaches to solving the inverse problem of reconstruction of the permittivity profile of multilayer dielectric structure developed by Ukrainian authors are under consideration. A number of resonator constructions for permittivity measurements suggested by Ukrainian scientist are analyzed. Some ideas for subsurface probing data processing are under discussion. The information about some original microwave components and devices, which can be applied for obtaining measuring instruments, is presented.
